name: storage-platform

scripts.typecheck: npm run typecheck -w web && tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.tests.json
scripts.db:migrate:e2e: dotenv -e .env.test -e .env.local -- npx prisma migrate deploy --schema packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma && dotenv -e .env.test -e .env.local -- node packages/db/prisma/seed.mts && dotenv -e .env.test -e .env.local -- tsx --tsconfig apps/web/tsconfig.json apps/web/scripts/seed-demo.mts
scripts.e2e:server: npm run build:test && npm run start:test

_postinstall_note: The Prisma client is build output (node_modules/.prisma/client, re-exported by @prisma/client) and nothing else generates it, so a clean checkout has no client at all and a CI or Vercel build fails with "@prisma/client did not initialize yet". This is the one place that makes a fresh `npm install` produce a working tree. It also generates the Linux engine named by binaryTargets, which is what the deployed functions load.
_overrides_note: Only transitive deps we can bump without putting the tree in an `invalid` state. Left alone deliberately: postcss/sharp (pinned by next), brace-expansion (minimatch@3 requires the 1.x line). `npm audit` runs in CI so the inherited advisories stay visible; they clear when next and eslint ship bumps.
